title: Woke up, wrote up a design document, two days of back and forth with Claude later I have a nearly finished demo.
author: RedTowerStudio
selftext:
Heyo people! My work has us using Claude now a bit more and I decided to give it's black magic a full shot at helping me make a game. I do have a background in programming, but not a lot of game dev experience. Most of what you see here was done with shaders, tweens, and procedural generation. It can sometimes be a pain to get what you want, but it really is a powerful tool! This was done in Godot 4.6, and all models were made in engine or via code. 

If anyone is interested in helping me test the multiplayer (it should be working it does with my own devices) the discord for the game is here [https://discord.gg/rS2YrFybf](https://discord.gg/rS2YrFybf)

comments.author: mskuchiki
comments.body:
i'd be interested in more details of this back and forth with claude and godot, more details on how you let claude interact with godot.

I've been searching for the best setup to integrate claude into godot, found mcps, skills, plugins, all of them had some vantages and disadvantages, hard to find someone who made a large project to really give advice on what is the best approach...

replies.author: RedTowerStudio
replies.body:
I find the best setup is to start with a solid design document - so first just lay out what architecture, patterns, tech, mechanics, etc etc you want. As clear as you can, preferably with sketches (I use asprite to make really bad doodles, those work it just needs guidance) and these go in an image reference folder. From there I will just slowly create detailed documents of what I want and dont want, what is allowed and not allowed, and let claude edit whatever it wants in Godot.   
  
I don't use an MCP yet, I follow MVVM patterns and use C# for the majority of the code. I use VS code for my IDE. If a model does need to be made I have found that Claude's MCP plugin to Blender is good if you have creative ways to build assets(I know there are other model generation options but idk, I still l can't bring myself to use them yet). If it can't do something, I find a tutorial. If there is only youtube tutorials, I have gemini summarize into a good super technical script, then I will teach Claude whatever it was messing up on and make SURE to add it to a design document that it must reference. 

I am not very deep yet into Claude's ecosystem in my opinion, so I doubt my approach is the best. But I can get some very nice results if I mix what I already know and Claude's speed.

replies.author: PaintingSilenc3
replies.body: So are you saying... Think before you act?!

replies.author: BrotherMoy
replies.body: No MCP? So are you copy and pasting all code blocks? How does Claude have any reference to your object set up? Or is it just giving you suggestions and you're doing all the manual input?

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: Godot doesn't need an MCP to interact with. Yes it can let Claude run in engine tests without writing up headless scripts, but all file creation/editing can be done manually as Godot's game files are all stored as text files anyway.

replies.author: BrotherMoy
replies.body: Yeah but what about the asset generation, shaders, etc. Are you just using VS code and connecting a model to your project and doing scene set ups manually?

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
Those assets are just text files in Godot too. Both procedural meshes and GLTFs are editable text. Shader files are text files. Etc. If you want to place objects, yes that would require your manual setup unless you want to hook up an mcp for that. But frankly Claude is bad at all of the aforementioned things as its visual and spatial capabilities are by far the weakest areas of the model. It can do it to some extent, but without a human to bridge the gap manually and tweak it/make adjustments it's going to be quite poor. A wheel might have squared edges that overlap, for instance, or grass might be floating 1m above the ground it's supposed to sit on.

It's actually pretty good with basic shaders, but if you want something custom that hasn't been done before in a game, or done rarely, then you're going to have to dig deep and either iterate a lot or do some serious manual work, but it won't make a difference if it has mcp or not in either case there.

Personally, I make most of my assets by hand and iterate a lot with Claude for certain assets that I want procedural setups for, because procedural work is outside my wheelhouse. I can craft a scene in blender from scratch much faster than Claude could make even a small piece of that scene, and it will be at a  much higher quality (meaning I don't need to go back and fix everything.) Claude IS very good at making sweeping changes though that I would struggle with. For instance shifting certain groups of assets over to other material palettes or applying a metallic sheen or emissive texture in certain places across the full scene. Tedious stuff, like that.

One trick I did find was that if you want Claude to actually make good looking stuff, you can boil it down to a voxel setup and get it to "draw" out a voxelized blueprint of something first. For instance, Claude can "perceive" ASCII maps in order to know where to put things. So you can get one agent to draw out an ASCII map (with provided instructions about a legend for, say, either map features or a platform level) and then you have a second agent take the maps that were drawn and implement them according to your guidelines into the actual game. Or just have it build a tool to convert your custom ASCII driven maps into whatever format your top-down or platform levels are.  Contextualizing a visual or spatial problem is probably the way to get the highest quality results (at least pre-Fable... Fable was impressing me while we had it, and might've convinced me to try passing off some of the asset gen to it.)

It's worse. It's trash. I mean it's cool that they were able to make anything at all. But to post this here being like wow look what I did. It looks gross, frankly. I wouldn't show this off if you paid me. 

Art wise, I think if leaning heavily on LLMs, which I also am, the only choice is put some hands on and make decent art yourself (very hard) or go full abstract art, full on lines and geometric shapes. Can still do a lot of sick games like that. But this foot submarine thing looks terrible.

Yeah. But all the portals are now like that, from CrazyGames to Kongregate. It's like a candy store with all games on your screen all at once. While playing a game, it shows all the other games you could be playing.
